text:
Sam K: FYI noticed a sharp uptick in hosted-GPU bill this morning + several customers crossed over into committed thresholds. spreadsheet: https://redwood-internal/ops/capacity-forecast — can we triage if we're short on reserved GPUs for next 30d?
Mia R: which region? anywhere specific or global trend?
Sam K: mostly us-west1 and eu-west1. us-west1 has the largest delta vs reserved.
Jonah P: pulling a quick projection from billing data now. I'll paste the query and output in a sec.
Jonah P: SQL I ran:```SELECT date, sum(gpu_hours) as gpu_hours, avg(p95_latency_ms) as p95 FROM `billing.gpu_usage` WHERE date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) GROUP BY date ORDER BY date;```
Jonah P: 30d avg GPU hours: us-west1=18,400h/day, eu-west1=9,200h/day. Current reserved capacity covers ~24,000h/day in total across regions. With committed contracts expiring mid-May, we project a shortfall of ~4,500h/day in us-west1 during peak windows.
Lia Chen: shortfall translates to how many gpus? (n1-standard-avg)
Jonah P: at 24h/day per GPU, 4,500h/day ≈ 188 GPUs. If we convert to cost delta on on-demand: delta = 188 * (on-demand_rate - reserved_rate) * 24 ≈ 188 * ($2.40 - $0.75) * 24 ≈ $7,560/day.
Mia R: ouch. finance ping?
billing-bot: @channel Alert: Unexpected increase in hourly GPU spend in project redwood-hosted-prod-us-west1. Estimated 7.6k USD/day incremental if no reserved capacity adjustment. Invoice link: https://billing.redwood/invoices/2026-03
Lia Chen: two quick options: 1) increase reserved commit for us-west1 for next quarter (lead-time ~7d for vendors) 2) shift some traffic to eu-west1/dedicated pools and enable autoscaled preemptibles as fallback for non-SLA workloads.
Sam K: what about reallocating burst capacity from low-usage regions? Any constraints on model locality?
Jonah P: we have ~320 spare GPUs in ap-southeast but currently several models are pinned to us-west1 for latency reasons. We could temporarily re-route async batch and embeddings to ap-southeast with a config change: set route.policy = "cost-first" for routes matching /batch and /embeds.
Sam K: can infra-oncall make that routing change? risk?
infra-oncall: I can flip route policy for non-SLA routes. Risk: increased latency for AP customers; need to add header-based routing and update CDN geo-preferences. Will open a change ticket and run canary for 2h.
Mia R: finance wants a formal 30/60/90 day cost projection before approving a mid-quarter commit. Jonah can you paste the projection table?
Jonah P: quick projection snapshot (30/60/90 days):
- 30d: shortfall 4,500h/day -> 188 GPUs -> incremental cost ~$7.6k/day
- 60d: expected demand growth +10% -> shortfall ~6,000h/day -> 250 GPUs -> incremental ~$10.1k/day
- 90d: growth +18% -> shortfall ~7,500h/day -> 312 GPUs -> incremental ~$12.6k/day
Mia R: these numbers assume on-demand fallback at current prices. If we negotiate a short-term committed add-on at a 20% discount vs listed reserved rate, break-even timelines change.
Sam K: action items: (1) Jonah finalize 30/60/90 table + CSV and drop in ops-shared (2) infra-oncall: prepare routing playbook to move /batch and /embeds (3) Lia sync with finance on short-term commit pricing and time-to-provision.
Lia Chen: I'll start an internal PR with vendor options and lead times, cc @Sam K.
Jonah P: uploaded CSV: https://redwood-internal/ops/forecast/1765432100-capacity-proj.csv (contains region breakout + hourly curves).
infra-oncall: opened change ticket CHG-84321 to flip routing for non-SLA canary. Target window: tonight 02:00-04:00 UTC.
Sam K: thanks. also, spike correlates with two new customers ramping their token volumes (details in the csv). If we can throttle or tag for non-commit traffic we can reduce immediate pressure.
Mia R: I'll add throttling flags to the onboarding flow for those installs (non-committed).
billing-bot: Note: Vendor invoice for reserved capacity due 2026-03-29. If commit changes are made after that date, we may be billed for excess on-demand until provisioning completes.
Sam K: good catch. keep everyone posted. If anyone sees any unexpected autoscaler behavior, ping infra-oncall. :thumbsup:
Lia Chen: will follow up with a vendor pricing matrix and recommend 3 commit packages (small/medium/large) optimized for break-even within 45 days.
Jonah P: final note — I'm also seeing a small network egress bump for embeddings to external customers in us-west1. If that persists, will open a separate billing ticket.
Sam K: ok. wrapping up: owners: Jonah (forecast + CSV), Lia (vendor + finance), infra-oncall (routing change + canary). Back in this thread with updates.
